template.tagline: Same rocket, but the booster flies home.
template.brief: Identical to Curlew, plus landing legs, grid fins, cold-gas thrusters and 35 t of propellant held back for the landing burn. That reserve and hardware cost about 4.5 t of payload. Reuse trades payload for hardware you get to fly again.

benchmark.class: Medium-lift kerolox with propulsive first-stage landing
benchmark.text: Propulsive landing of an orbital-class booster became routine in the late 2010s. The booster keeps propellant in reserve for boost-back, entry and landing burns, which is why reusable missions carry noticeably less than expendable ones.
